title: Stress Coping Style
description: Understand how you respond to a crisis. Do you take action right away, look for emotional support, or run away?

questions.cop_1: I focus all my effort on finding a way to deal with the problem.
questions.cop_2: I quickly make a plan with concrete steps for what I need to do.
questions.cop_3: I get emotional support, sympathy, or understanding from people close to me.
questions.cop_4: I look for someone to talk to so I can let out my feelings about what happened.
questions.cop_5: I use alcohol, drugs, or sleep all day to forget about the stress.
questions.cop_6: I spend time gaming, watching TV, or scrolling social media to escape the problem.
questions.cop_7: I try to find expert information or specific advice on how to handle this problem.
questions.cop_8: I take strong action to try to get rid of the source of the problem right away.
questions.cop_9: I find comfort in religion, prayer, or meditation and other spiritual activities.
questions.cop_10: I try to see this bad event from a different angle so it looks more positive (finding the lesson).
questions.cop_11: I deny that the problem is really happening (playing dumb / denial).
questions.cop_12: I deliberately refuse to believe that something this bad just happened to me.
questions.cop_13: I try to figure out which strategies I need to change in myself to get through this crisis.
questions.cop_14: I look for someone who will listen to my worries with full empathy.
questions.cop_15: I vent my frustration by lashing out or taking my emotions out on the wrong things.
questions.cop_16: I give up mentally on trying to resolve this crisis (feeling fate is too cruel).
questions.cop_17: I set aside my other activities and cancel my downtime so I can focus on this problem.
questions.cop_18: I laugh at my problems and respond with dark jokes or satire.
questions.cop_19: I turn my attention to other work or projects so I don't have to face the main crisis.
questions.cop_20: I accept that this crisis has happened and try to validate the pain I'm feeling.

results.description: When stressed, you focus on finding real solutions and changing the situation.
You put social support and emotional validation first so you feel calmer before acting.
You tend to escape reality through entertainment, denial, or sleep to bury the problem for a while.
